# command reference), translated to Neovim keybindings and :Skg*

# for every binding named here; if this file and that module disagree,
# keymaps.lua wins. Where COMMANDS.org describes Emacs-only mechanics
# (the minibuffer, magit), the text below is rewritten for the nvim
# equivalents (vim command-line prompts, neogit / plain git-diff

* user-facing skg commands
** :w : :SkgSave
Each time you save, your view is rebuilt.
This is because you can put 'requests' into your view,
in which you request more data,
such as a node's ancestors, or the nodes that link to it.
Since views can overlap,
saving one open view can change another
(see "what a save does to other views" below).
You may edit several views at once, but Neovim asks when an edit
first dirties a view while another view already has unsaved edits;
choosing Cancel restores the view's last clean text. On save, Skg checks the other dirty
views' last clean text and current text against every graph identity the
prepared save can affect, except through a link: a node that only links
to a saved node, or that a saved node only links to, does not count, since
a link holds no copy of its target. A conflict is a hard refusal before any write;
the error names the views and IDs. Missing or malformed baseline data is
also refused conservatively. There is no "save anyway" choice.

Each view also keeps the text the server last drew for it, its
baseline, and sends it with every save. A save is refused, before any
write, if a node you edited or deleted in the view has changed since
the server drew the view: by a save from another client or from
'tools/skg-for-ai', which this client's views do not follow, or by
another writer of the '.skg' files (a second server over the same
data, a 'git pull', an editor), which the server reloads as the files
change. The server compares the view's copy of each node with the
graph, so only real changes count: a node the view shows as the graph
has it is not written, however old the view; and a restart, a rebuild
or a whitespace strip makes no view stale by itself. A node that
changed but that you did not edit, which the view still shows as the
server drew it, refuses nothing: the save leaves it as the graph has
it, writes the rest, and warns "Left as the graph has it: TITLE (ID),
which changed after this buffer was rendered and which this buffer did
not edit." (or "which was deleted after ..." for a node the graph no
longer has); the redrawn view shows the graph's version. A node the
view writes without having been drawn in it (pasted in by ID, or typed
into a new empty view) is not checked.
The error names each such node, the view's headlines for it, and what
changed in it since the view was drawn: the title (old and new), the
body (with its changed lines, then against now), the content (the IDs
gained and lost), the home skgrepo (old and new), or by name its
aliases, extra IDs, flags, forks or hides; or that
the node was deleted. Your edits stay in the view: archive them if
needed (:SkgShowUnsavedChanges), open a fresh view, and reapply them.

Only a changed node you edited or deleted refuses a save, and the
refusal is whole: nothing the buffer asks is written, not even its
edits of nodes nobody else changed. Recovering is a reconciliation
by hand of two diffs from one common base, the text the server last drew:
the recovery document holds your edits as a diff against that text,
and the error holds the graph's change against the same text. To
recover a view, keeping all of its roots:
- Copy the buffer's text aside: ':SkgShowUnsavedChanges' writes it,
  with a diff against the text the server last drew, to a file.
- Discard the buffer's edits and redraw it: mark it unmodified
  (':set nomodified'), then ':SkgRerenderAllViews', which redraws
  every open view without unsaved edits from the graph as it now is,
  with all of its roots. It never redraws a buffer that still has
  unsaved edits: it leaves that buffer as it is and names it in a
  notification, so marking the buffer unmodified is what lets it go.
- Reapply your diff by hand over the new text, where it still
  applies; where the graph changed the same lines (the error shows
  how), decide what the text should say.
(Emacs: the same, with M-~ and M-x skg-request-rerender-all-views.)

When the server reloads files changed on disk, it says so in a
notification, naming each skgrepo and how many of its files it
reloaded ("skg: reloaded 2 files from repo first"), and rerenders
every open view showing a changed node that holds no unsaved edits.
A buffer of the diff view so rerendered is also extended to the
changes it did not show, as <localleader>ru would extend it.
When something could not be reloaded (a file it could not read,
say), the whole notice goes instead to the server-warnings buffer
(=skg://messages/server-warnings=), under "Repo changes", which is
shown. A view with unsaved edits keeps them, and its save
is refused if you edited a changed node in it. No rebuild is needed after
a 'git pull'. A changed config still needs one (':SkgRebuildSessionLifetimeStores').

':w' is the BufWriteCmd on every skg view buffer, so plain saving
works as expected; ':SkgSave' does the same thing as an explicit
Ex command.

If the current files for anything being saved select a title or body
from below that node's home, Skg stops before every write and offers
*Hoist* or *Abort*. Hoist moves the selected text to home, removes
lower title/body copies, and preserves lower relationships and aliases;
the exact approved PIDs are reread and rechecked as one batch before the
save proceeds. Abort leaves every file byte-for-byte unchanged. Scripts
and maintenance writers have no prompt and refuse this repair.

That disk-publication choice is separate from displaying the result. If
a successful save under a skgrepo restriction would rerender text from
an overPrivateText telescope, Skg asks for a second, request-scoped approval. Approve
and Skg asks the server for the rerender it withheld, of the saved view
and the other views the save changed; the save is not sent again. Decline
leaves the save skgsave-committed and the buffers as they were: the saved
buffer still holds what was saved, unrendered. Do not save it again:
the save would apply a second time. Its edits of existing nodes would
write nothing, but a new node it put under a container would make that
container stale and edited, refusing the save, and a new root of the view would be
created twice. Reopen the view to go on.
*** what a save does to other views
A save rerenders every other open view that shows what it changed,
and brings it up to date with the graph, saying nothing of what it
changed there. A child the graph no longer relates to its parent
vanishes from that view, with everything under it, wherever its
parent reads claims: one that another view's save removed from its
parent's content, say. A member that one view's save added is drawn
into every other view that shows its list, as a fresh view draws its
members: editable where no other occurrence of its node is and the
node budget allows, and then, unless it is a member of a forks
folder, with its forks folder when it has a fork partner, either way, the skgrepo restriction shows. A headline
standing for a node the save deleted vanishes from every content
view, with whatever stood under it; in the diff view it becomes the
node's ghost.
*** where a save's warnings go
A save's own warnings and errors go to a buffer of their own,
replaced at each save that has any: =skg://messages/save-warnings=,
=skg://messages/save-errors= when the save was refused, or
=skg://messages/save-errors-and-warnings= when it has both. One such
warning names each orphan graphnode the save created: a node that no
list contains, made from a headline typed under a parent that reads
no claims ('docs/glossary.org', "claims membership", lists those
parents). A new view root is in no list either, but is not warned
of.

A rerender that follows a command (<localleader>vl, a commit, an
import, the cleanup of references to an absent node, the extension of
the diff view, or ':SkgRerenderAllViews') has errors and warnings of
its own, which go to =skg://messages/rerender=.
** :SkgRerenderAllViews : redraw every clean view
Redraws every open view that has no unsaved edits from the graph as it
now is, each with all of its roots; a buffer of the diff view is
refreshed. A view with unsaved edits is left as it is, since the server
draws a view from what it last rendered or saved, and the redraw would
discard the edits; a notification names each one skipped. See ":w"
for its use after a refused save. (Emacs: M-x
skg-request-rerender-all-views.)
** :SkgShowUnsavedChanges : archive edits for manual recovery
Prompts for a local Org file, writes a detached recovery document, opens
it, and reports its actual path. The document contains context, lossless
JSON strings for the clean baseline and current text, and a readable
unified diff. It does not save graph data, close or clean the source view,
or register the archive as a live view.

When a save is refused, archive the relevant dirty views, close those live
views, save the remaining view, reopen fresh views, and manually reapply
the intended edits. Do not save an entire stale archived copy over the
newer graph.
** <localleader>dd : deletion
***     <localleader>dd : :SkgDelete
Marks the node at point for deletion from the graph.
Upon saving the view, it will vanish not just from this view,
but from the graph itself.
On a fork of yours drawn in place of its original (marked 'ĥ') as
content of someone else's note, it deletes the fork and leaves their note as it
was, unforked, drawing the original again where the fork stood. Under
a note of yours it takes the original out of your note too
('docs/forks.org', "Taking back a fork").
Under a skgrepo restriction, when relationships recorded in skgrepos
the skgrepo restriction keeps out name the deleted node (another node's
private section contains it, say), the save writes nothing and asks
"Delete from: (c)ancel, (v)isible records only, (a)ll owned records",
saying how many such relationships there are. Visible records only
deletes the node and the relationships you can see, and leaves the
others as they are, so the node's ID dangles there; all owned records
removes them too, as a save with no skgrepo restriction does. Cancel
saves nothing. The choice applies to that save alone.
*** <localleader>dR : :SkgDeleteRecursive
Same as Delete, but also marks every occurrence viewdescendant
of the node at point. Descendent headlines that are not occurrences
(ghosts, unknown viewnodes, aliasFolder, idFolder, etc.) are skipped.

Its own binding, not a prefix-arg variant -- nvim has no prefix-arg
protocol to reuse here the way Emacs's C-u did. Call it directly as
<localleader>dR, or as ':SkgDeleteRecursive'.
*** :SkgStripAttribution
On a fork, asks the next save to remove its attribution, as
skg-strip-attribution does in Emacs ('docs/forks.org',
"Attribution"). No binding; does not save.
*** <localleader>da : :SkgDeleteReferencesToAbsentNode
On an unknown viewnode, remove that exact raw ID from owned structured
relationships throughout retained telescopes, then refresh only views which
show a changed recorder or that exact raw ID.
The command refuses while a view is dirty.  Text links are reported but left
unchanged, and require confirmation before the structural cleanup.  If the
scan changes before confirmation, the command refuses the stale approval;
run it again to rescan.  The warning ends by naming
':SkgInvestigateUnknownNode' (<localleader>tr), which shows what git
history knows of the ID.
Under a skgrepo restriction it refuses ("Deleting the references to an
absent ID requires no skgrepo restriction"), since it rewrites every
owned recorder, those the skgrepo restriction keeps out included.
** <localleader>f : text search
The 'f' is for 'find'.
*** <localleader>ff : :SkgSearch
Text search across titles and aliases, returning every
matching node. Prominent nodes (roots, cycle members,
mentioned nodes, and nodes that had an org-roam ID before import)
are bumped in the ranking via their prominence multiplier.

A node with =NoSearchMatching= cannot be a direct title, alias, or body hit
in any search mode. It may still appear as context for another hit and remains
openable by ID. This is decluttering, not privacy. A packing list mentioning
“shaver,” for example, can be excluded while the shaver node still matches.

Prompts for search terms. All search axes take their conservative
defaults: no per-token regex, titles only (no body), no Tantivy
phrase and operator syntax.

Under a skgrepo restriction, if the search index contains any overPrivateText
telescope (one whose selected title or body lies below home), Skg asks
whether to include or exclude overPrivateText telescopes before running the query.
Exclude filters them in Tantivy before matching, and from what is drawn
under each hit; Include is permission
for this search only. With no skgrepo restriction they are included
without a prompt and the result carries a warning.

The hits come best first, each a write-protected headline showing
its node's title. Under each hang, folded, its containers folder,
whose members carry their own containers up to the roots, and,
when there are any, its forks folder, flat: the nodes it forks, those
that fork it, then its other mirrors, each with its own containers
folder. A hit found through an alias shows those
folders collapsed and its alias folder open, holding all of the
node's aliases, the matching one among them. The search buffer
arrives whole, in one answer, and is an ordinary view.

Run 'Goto' (<localleader>gg, below) from one of the links in the
search results to open the view from that node.
*** <localleader>fi : :SkgSearchInteractive (search-interactive)
Same as Search, but after the search terms it prompts:

: Type a character for each search option: (r)egex, (b)ody, (t)antivy syntax, (h)elp:

Type one character for each option you want, in any order,
then press Enter. An empty answer uses the same conservative
defaults as ':SkgSearch'. Unrecognized characters are ignored.
Typing =h= opens this documentation (docs/COMMANDS-nvim.org,
falling back to docs/COMMANDS.org if that file is missing), with
all folds opened and the cursor searched onto this headline -- and
abandons the search. If the headline can't be found the whole file
is still shown, with a notice that the search failed.

- =r= (*regex*) — per-token regex instead of phrase search.
  Bypasses the query parser; each whitespace-separated piece
  is handed to Tantivy's 'RegexQuery'.
- =b= (*body*) — also search the body field (titles are
  always searched).
- =t= (*tantivy syntax*) — Tantivy phrase and operator syntax
  (AND/OR/NOT/+/-). In non-regex mode this passes through
  Tantivy's QueryParser (phrase quotes, grouping, field: all
  work; intra-word operator chars get escaped so =foo:bar=
  remains findable). In regex mode, AND / OR / NOT / +foo /
  -bar combine the per-piece RegexQueries at the document
  level; phrase syntax does not apply there. See the regex=true
  section below.
**** Query syntax with default axes (phrase/operators=false, regex=false)
Queries are literal. The query string is split on whitespace,
and any word containing a Tantivy operator character
(=+ - & | ! ( ) { } [ ] ^ " ~ * ? : \=) or the bare keyword
=AND= / =OR= / =NOT= is wrapped as a phrase so its contents
are searched literally. Words without specials pass through.
- *OR between words*. "dog cat" matches titles containing
  either word; a title with both outranks one with only one.
- *Literal special characters*. A title like "C++ tips",
  "[draft] plan", or "cat:dog" is findable by typing its
  literal text.
**** Query syntax with phrase/operators=true
The query is handed to Tantivy's QueryParser, with one
heuristic adjustment: any operator character sitting strictly
inside a word (with word chars on both sides, scanning
through consecutive operators within the same token) is
backslash-escaped. So =foo:bar= stays findable as a literal,
but =AND= / =OR= / =+foo= / =-bar= / ="fox in socks"= /
=(dog OR cat)= keep their operator meaning.

Known imperfection: the heuristic can't distinguish a
configured field name from a user word, so
=title_or_alias:dog= gets its =:= escaped too. Field-
qualified queries need manual =\:= in operators mode.
**** Query syntax with regex=true
The query is split on whitespace and each piece is handed to
'tantivy::query::RegexQuery' as its own pattern. Matches are
against *tokens*, not raw text: the indexer lowercases and
splits on whitespace, so no stored token ever contains a
space. That's why splitting is the only way multi-word regex
queries return anything. Patterns like =histor.*= work for
prefix search ('history', 'historical'), and =polit.* scien.*=
combines two such prefix searches. Combine with body=true to
also search body fields.

The *=*= gotcha*: in regex =*= means "zero or more of the
previous character", not "any characters" (that's =.*=). So
=sci*= matches the tokens =sc=, =sci=, =scii=, … — not
"anything starting with sci". Use =sci.*= for that.

With operators=false, pieces are OR'd (SHOULD-combined)
like the non-regex default.

With phrase/operators=true (the wire flag is still
=operators=true=), the keywords =AND= / =OR= / =NOT= and the
prefixes =+piece= / =-piece= combine the per-piece RegexQueries
at the document level:
- =poli.* AND sci.*= — documents whose tokens include one
  matching =poli.*= and one matching =sci.*=.
- =poli.* NOT bio.*= — documents matching =poli.*= and not
  any token matching =bio.*=.
- =+poli.* -bio.*= — same as above, without the keywords.
- =poli.* OR sci.*= — explicit OR, same as the default.
Keywords are consumed rather than matched as patterns. An
=AND= adjacent to a piece on either side promotes that piece
to MUST.
**** Caveats
- Each alias is indexed as its own document, so a query can
  match on an alias even when the title doesn't mention the
  searched word. The returned node is still the aliased one.
- Results are ranked by BM25 times a prominence multiplier
  (Root 100×, CycleMember ~32×, Mentioned 10×, HadID 10×,
  MultiContained ~3.2×, everything else 1×). A weaker text
  match on a root can outrank a stronger match on a leaf,
  but every match is returned — search is never filtered by
  graph role.
- Regex distance is tokenwise: a pattern never spans
  whitespace, because we split the query on whitespace before
  handing the pieces to RegexQuery. A true whole-title regex
  (one pattern that matches across spaces) would need a
  separate non-tokenized =raw_title= field. Not done yet.
*** <localleader>fl : :SkgSearchMakeLink
Search-then-link: pick a result, return here, get a link.

Like ':SkgSearch' but tailored for inserting a link to a node
you don't yet know the ID of. The buffer and cursor position you
called it from are remembered. The same conservative search
defaults as ':SkgSearch' apply.

As in the Emacs client, the source buffer is not saved before
the search runs -- only its position is recorded. (Saving first
can let the server's rerender collapse a freshly typed blank
line, leaving the remembered position dangling on the next
headline, so the inserted link would glue itself to the wrong
spot.) Save your own edits first if you want them preserved
before detouring into the search.

In the resulting search buffer, find the result you want and
press <CR> (or <localleader>cc). The search buffer closes; you
return to the buffer you started in, at the position you were at;
and a =[[id:X][LABEL]]= link is inserted at point.

The label is the result's title with any inline links inside
it reduced to their labels (so the new link's label is plain
text, never another link inside a link).
** <localleader>g : going to a node
*** <localleader>gg : :SkgGoto
Calling this when the cursor is on a link, a node's metadata,
a bare UUID, or a .skg filename
will open a new view from the ID it finds there,
or go to the content view of it that was already open if that exists
(a buffer of the diff view does not count: the node gets a new view).

The requested node itself is the root, as itself: a fresh view is
drawn from the root homes, where the root's own skgrepo decides. A
perspective switch (=<localleader>vo=) may show another mirror there.
Content below it substitutes. Fork facts remain
visible in its heralds (the K token).

If you're not sure whether the cursor is on something visitable
(a link or a node's metadata),
use IdNext and IdPrev (the ]i / [i motions, or <localleader>in /
<localleader>ip)
to identify where those are.
*** <localleader>GG : :SkgGotoAndCloseThis
Like Goto, but also closes the buffer it was called from.
*** <localleader>gb : :SkgGotoBiggestBranch
Go to the branch near point with the most recursive content,
estimated by counting viewdescendants in the current buffer.

If the node at point has siblings, this considers that sibling
set. If it has no siblings, it considers the node's immediate
children instead.

This can help when a view is loading slowly:
replacing the content relationship to its biggest branch
with a link relationship (<localleader>ml)
reduces the view's demands on the server.
*** <localleader>gi : :SkgGotoById
'Goto' is usually more convenient.

This requires a literal v4 UUID string, like
3861db2c-7f16-4814-b403-52b5e05d5e0a
It can be useful going from git to skg.
*** <localleader>Gi : :SkgGotoByIdAndCloseThis
*** <localleader>gm : :SkgGotoInGit
Opens a neogit status view of the changes to the file containing
the node at point. If the file appears in multiple sections
(unstaged, staged, untracked), point lands on the first and
the user is warned. (If neogit is unavailable, this falls back
to the plain git-diff view described below.)
*** <localleader>Gm : :SkgGotoInGitAndCloseThis
*** <localleader>gM : :SkgGotoInGitParent
Opens a plain git-diff buffer (named =skg://git-diff/FILE=) of
the *parent*'s file -- the combined staged+unstaged diff, or the
untracked file's own content if it has no HEAD diff -- with point
on the first line in that buffer containing this node's ID.
Warns if the ID appears multiple times. (Emacs's magit has an API
for landing on a specific line within a status section; neogit
doesn't, so this variant uses a plain diff buffer instead of a
neogit view -- same information, different chrome.)
*** <localleader>GM : :SkgGotoInGitParentAndCloseThis
*** <localleader>gv : :SkgGotoViewnodeId
Moves the cursor to the headline carrying a viewnode ID, read from
the prompt. A message names each headline it concerns by its
viewnode ID, with this command: "To find it: <localleader>gv X". It
finds the headline while heralds conceal its metadata, and opens the
folds around it. See =docs/api-and-formats.org=, "How a message
names a headline".
** <localleader>t : git operations
*** <localleader> (g|G)(m|M) : :SkgGotoInGit*
These four commands are described elsewhere in this document.
*** <localleader>tr         : :SkgInvestigateUnknownNode
The twin of Emacs's skg-investigate-unknown-node. Says what git
history knows of an unknown graphnode: one that an ID in some list
names and no graphnode answers to, which a view shows as an unknown
viewnode, heralded "Reference to unknown node.". On an unknown
viewnode it takes that ID; anywhere else it asks for one. The answer opens read-only in
=skg://unknown-node=, as Org text. If the ID resolves to a node, it
names that node, its ID and its home skgrepo. Otherwise it searches
the git history (first parents, from HEAD) of every skgrepo, and
reports the most recent commit that held the ID's file, the commit it
vanished at, its title then, its own relation lists then, and every
node that referred to it then, links included; or that the ID was
never in any skgrepo's history. If HEAD still holds the ID's file,
it says so: "still present at HEAD (only the worktree lacks it)". It
refuses unless the connection is unrestricted; a refusal opens the
same buffer, as "* investigation failed" with the reason under it.
** <localleader>l : show a folder (both folders of a relation)
These commands don't edit the graph. Each inserts a request into the
metadata of the node at point that, on save, causes the server to
render the relation's folder viewnodes into the view, populated from
the graph. Each builds both folders of its relation (but containers and
mentioners build one, as do aliases and flags, which are no relation).
Under each member of a partner folder hangs its containerward chain,
under a member of the forksFolder in a folded containers folder of its
own (see <localleader>lc). The write-protected folder ☮
marks a folder you cannot change from here. Every command auto-saves.
Without such a request, an editable node shows only its forksFolder,
where it has a fork partner, either way, unless it is itself a member
of a forksFolder, which lists every mirror already (plus, on an
editable member of a forksFolder, the nonempty
integratedElsewhereFolder and hiddenInForkPartnerFolder, and on an
editable forker of the folder's node the nonempty
hiddenByForkerFolder); the heralds advertise other
nonempty relations. <localleader>lf on a member of a forksFolder draws its own.

In a content view, each node a forksFolder holds that the node forks
(a forkee as such, =bK= or =bKb=) is drawn editable, as content is,
unless it is editable elsewhere in the buffer or the node budget is
spent: it shows its content less what the node contains or hides,
and less what another node you own contains, and its own folders,
first among them the folder of what it contains that you keep
elsewhere ("☮ It contains these, and you keep them elsewhere."),
folded and write-protected, each member with a folded containers
folder naming where you keep it. Its title and body save when you
own it; a foreign one's edits are refused (view it as itself, where
an edit starts the fork operation).
Deleting one of its children hides it in the forking node, unless a
node you own (the forking node, or another) contains it after the
save: moving a child into a node of yours hides nothing; a headline
typed under it, or a node moved there from elsewhere, joins its
content, after the child it follows, when you own it, and is refused
under a foreign one.

Each node a forksFolder holds that the node does not fork (a forker
as such, claiming nothing: one that forks the node, =Kb=, or an
indirect member, a mirror of the node joined to it only through
others, with no 'b' flag) is drawn the same way: editable unless a
repeat or past the budget, showing what a member shows (its content
less what the node contains or hides, and less what another node you
own contains), with its own folders. Under it,
first, stands the folder of what it contains that you keep elsewhere,
then the folder of what the node hides of its content ("☮ It
contains these, but c hides them."), then,
under one that forks the node, the folder of what it hides of the
node's content ("☮ a hides these, which c contains."), each folded
and write-protected. Its title and body save when you own it, and are
refused when it is foreign; a headline typed under it, or a node
moved there, joins its content when you own it. A save never reads its partial content as
its whole list. Deleting one of its children (a cut) makes the
node fork it, so it is redrawn claiming, among the forkees (a mutual,
=bKb=, where it forks the node), without its folder of what it hides
of the node's content (drawn under a forker only); the node hides the child unless
the node, or another node you own, contains it after the save, so a
child cut there and pasted into the node's own content, or into any
node of yours, is taken in, hiding nothing. Under a
foreign node such a save is refused.
*** <localleader>la : :SkgShowFolderOfAliases
The aliasFolder -- other text you could search for to find this node
(you can always search for its title; most nodes have none). Writable:
type an alias in and save.
*** <localleader>lh : :SkgShowFolderOfHides
The hiderFolder and hiddenFolder -- both write-protected (☮). Hiding is edited from
a member as such, the forks folder, or the folder of what a note hides
outside its fork partners, never from these folders. On a node that neither
hides nor is hidden, nothing appears.
*** <localleader>lf : :SkgShowFolderOfForks
The forksFolder, editable and shown even when empty: first the nodes
this node forks, in its list's order, each claiming membership (=bK=;
a mutual, which also forks this node, =bKb=); then the nodes that fork
this one and that it neither forks nor hides, each claiming nothing
(=Kb=), by the order of their home skgrepos in your config; then
every other mirror of this node that it does not hide (a fork of
what it forks, say), each claiming nothing, nearest first, with no
'b' flag; last, the folder of what this node hides outside its fork
partners, when it hides any: what no member of the forks folder,
forkee, forker or other mirror, contains (a hide a member contains stands under
that member instead, in its folder of what this node hides in it).
The folder is flat: no member shows a forks folder of its own unless
asked (this command, on the member). Typing a member in, or attaching a
forker (<localleader>sa), makes this node fork it. Deleting a member
it forks stops the fork; detaching a mutual stops only the fork;
deleting a mutual, a forker or another mirror also hides it, so that it moves to the
hidden-outside folder, whence deleting it unhides it. Deleting a
"restricted" member (one the skgrepo restriction keeps out), in
either folder, changes nothing, and it is drawn again.
*** <localleader>lp : :SkgShowFolderOfFlags
Shows the write-protected, true-only flags folder as titleless viewnodes whose
heralds carry their labels, in canonical order.
The empty folder is retained. Import provenance viewnodes have no setter; use the
search-matching command below for =No search matching=. Delete the whole
folder branch to dismiss this optional view without changing any flag.
*** <localleader>lc : :SkgShowFolderOfContainers
The containerFolder -- the nodes that contain this one, but for those
the view already shows above it. Write-protected (☮):
containment is edited from the container. Its other side, the node's
content, is shown without a folder. On a node nothing else contains,
nothing appears, and the save's warnings say "No other containers.",
naming it. Under each member of this folder, and of every other partner
folder but the diff view's two acquisition folders, hangs its
containerward chain: the member's containers, write-protected and
claiming nothing, theirs under them, up to the roots or
'max_roleTree_depth', a container met again on the way shown once
more as a leaf. A request on a chain node draws that node's own
containers folder. A fresh content view shows its root's containers
folder this way. Under a member of a forksFolder the chain stands in a
containerFolder instead, drawn folded (only its headline shows; open
it to see the member's containers, but those the view shows above
it), so that a fork partner's containers do not look like its
content; the diff view hangs the chain directly. A member that
repeats a node shown editable elsewhere in the buffer gets nothing.
A view drawn before this rule shows the old chain directly under such
a member, as content it cannot account for; reopen the view to
redraw it.
*** <localleader>lm : :SkgShowFolderOfMentioners
The mentionerFolder -- the nodes that link to this one. Write-protected
(☮): a link lives in the linking node's text. On a node nothing links to,
nothing appears.
** <localleader>s : setting node properties
*** first some vocab: 'editable' and 'write-protected'
A view of a node can be editable or write-protected.
Typically the first place in the buffer that depicts a node
is the editable view of it. So that other views of that node
cannot contradict it, they are 'write-protected': Edits to them
cannot affect the node they depict. One also has no content --
the server extends none under it,
in order to prevent the view from becoming redundant and huge --
but it may keep children, which claim nothing there (see below).

A write-protected occurrence saves nothing of its own,
so an edit to it refuses the whole save, and nothing is written:
a changed title or home skgrepo;
an alias folder lacking or reordering its aliases,
or one with a relRepo request;
or a flags folder that differs from the graph.
The refusal names the occurrence and what differs.
No child of a write-protected occurrence claims membership,
whatever it carries, and nothing in one of its folders does.
A child the user typed under it, which stays unwarranted (⊥),
since no save reads claims there, is still saved as a node of its
own: an orphan graphnode, a node that no list contains, of which the
save warns. A write-protected occurrence is one of the parents that
read no claims, which 'docs/glossary.org' lists under "claims
membership".
The way out is to make the edit at the node's editable occurrence
instead, or to undo it, make this occurrence editable
(<localleader>se on it), save, and edit it then.
*** PITFALL: Don't make something 'editable' by directly editing its metadata.
Instead, use 'SetEditable' (<localleader>se), below.
That's because Skg has to make other occurrences of it
(in this same buffer -- and maybe in the future other buffers too)
write-protected. That's because a buffer can only be saved
if it has at most one editable occurrence of a node.
Otherwise, two editable nodes could contradict each other.

Making a node write-protected is likewise a request
('RequestWriteProtected' (<localleader>sw), below), which the server
performs: the children of the write-protected occurrence then claim
nothing, since a write-protected occurrence has no content.
*** <localleader>se : :SkgSetEditable
If you want to see the editable view of that node
from a place where it is currently shown in a write-protected form,
call this function. It will make the current editable view
(if it exists) write-protected, keeping what it shows
(though no longer as its content: no child claims membership
under a write-protected occurrence), and then make an editable view here.
Moving editability back to that occurrence later
makes those children its content again.
Called on a node that is already editable,
it extends the node's content editable,
up to 'initial_node_limit' extensions,
and the members as such in its forksFolder too
(one an earlier server drew write-protected, say).
A buffer may carry only one such request per node.
It does not save; the request takes effect at the next save.
*** <localleader>sw : :SkgRequestWriteProtected
Requests that this occurrence become write-protected,
as described above. It does not save.
At the next save, edits the occurrence carries are saved first;
then the server makes it write-protected,
resyncing its title from the graph;
its children then claim nothing,
so that edits to its title, body or children no longer affect it
  (although edits to its children still affect those children:
  they keep their own editability, and their own content).
On an occurrence that is already write-protected, it does nothing.
In one save with <localleader>se on another occurrence of the same
node, it moves editability there.
The two requests on the same occurrence contradict each other,
and the save is refused.
*** <localleader>sW : :SkgRequestWriteProtectedRecursive
The same, for the occurrence and its whole content subtree:
every node in it becomes write-protected,
and no child under them claims membership.
*** <localleader>st : :SkgDetach
Under a parent that reads claims -- an editable occurrence, or a
folder under one that is not write-protected -- writes 'noClaim' on
the headline at point, so that the next save takes it out of the
parent's list. The headline stays in the buffer: a child the graph
put there shows =detach= until the save, and =⊥= after it.
Under a parent that reads no claims (a write-protected occurrence
or folder, a ghost, an unknown viewnode, a restricted viewnode, a
tombstone, or none at all; 'docs/glossary.org', "claims
membership", is the list) it refuses, since no child claims
membership there ("Cannot detach: the parent reads no claims ...").
On a headline whose kind claims nothing anywhere (a folder, a flag,
a tombstone, a change viewnode of the diff view) it refuses too
("Cannot detach: a headline of this kind (KIND) claims no membership"). On
a headline that claims nothing already, it says so and changes
nothing. It does not save.
*** <localleader>sa : :SkgAttach
The reverse of <localleader>st: removes 'noClaim' from the headline
at point. On a pending detachment, a headline the graph puts in the
parent's list and that shows =detach=, it cancels the detachment:
=detach= goes at once, and the next save keeps the headline in the
list ("Attached: the detachment is cancelled; the next save keeps
this headline in its parent's list."). On any other headline, one
shown =⊥= because the graph does not put it there, the next save puts
it in the parent's list ("Attached: the next save puts this headline
in its parent's list."), and the headline keeps its =⊥= until the
save. It refuses where <localleader>st does, with the same messages,
and on a headline that claims membership already it says so and
changes nothing. It does not save. The metadata editor (<localleader>vm) offers
'noClaim' as well.
*** <localleader>ss : :SkgSetRepo
Changes the skgrepo of the node at point.
The prompt starts with the current skgrepo as editable command-line
text. You can type the new skgrepo name directly,
or use S-Left / S-Right to cycle through owned skgrepos;
TAB completes among all configured skgrepo names.

The Emacs client's C-? helper (which opened an org buffer listing
every skgrepo from inside the minibuffer) has no cmdline analog --
few terminals deliver C-? reliably -- so it's dropped; run
':SkgViewRepoList' beforehand (or afterward) instead. It shows
the same thing: an org buffer listing every configured skgrepo name
as a headline, with that skgrepo's path as the headline body.

The command only edits the node's metadata in the current buffer.
Until the save, the headline's herald shows the move,
as =⌂:NEW= ([[./heralds.org][the heralds docs]], "Other heralds").
Save the view afterward (':w') to apply the move.

A write-protected occurrence is not changed -- the save would
refuse its skgrepo edit -- and produces a loud WARNING,
with the full ID list in ':messages'.

What the move does to the relationships touching the moved nodes, the
save decides, whether or not the view shows them. One it would leave
more public than a node's new home (an inbound relationship of a move
to a more private skgrepo) is raised to that home, and the save's
warnings say so. If it would leave others at their old, more private
skgrepos, it saves nothing yet: it lists them and asks whether to
reset all of them to their new defaults, none, or each in turn;
then it saves with that answer, or not at all if you quit.
*** <localleader>sS : :SkgSetRepoRecursive
Like 'SetRepo', but it also
changes the skgrepo of every content descendent of the node at point
whose skgrepo matches the original skgrepo of the node at point.
Only member descendents (those without the 'noClaim' atom) are traversed.
The write-protected warning and the save's handling of relationships
described under <localleader>ss apply here too, across the whole
subtree.
*** <localleader>sr : :SkgSetRelRepo
Sets the relRepo of the relationship the headline at point represents
-- =contains= for a content child, the folder's relation for a member
of an editable partner folder, or the alias membership for an alias
headline. An unknown viewnode or a restricted viewnode in one of
those writable positions is supported too: it carries only
its raw member ID, never a node edit.

For a node-to-node relationship, the command asks the server for its
default relRepo and current relRepo (the "relRepo info" endpoint; the
request names the relationship's recorder -- the viewparent, or the
folder's viewparent -- its member and its relation), then prompts
-- with TAB completion and S-Left/S-Right cycling, like the other
skgrepo prompts -- over the skgrepos at least as private as the
default (more public ones could leak an endpoint's ID and would be
refused at save), plus a no-override choice. The prompt starts with a
pending request when it is offered, else the current relRepo or the
default, so Enter keeps the most specific choice. If the server
cannot resolve the relationship (e.g. a node not yet saved), every
skgrepo is offered and the save's floor check backstops. For an
alias, the default is its owning node's home, read from the buffer
with no request.

Choosing a skgrepo writes an =(editRequest (relRepo REPO))= request,
which both raises privacy above the default and lowers it back down
to (never below) the default. The no-override choice removes the
request: a saved relationship keeps its saved skgrepo (sticky); to
reach the default, choose it.

The command only edits the buffer; save the view to apply it.
**** what <localleader>sr refuses
It writes nothing, and says why, where the headline at point
represents no relationship it can set. The messages are those of
the Emacs client's C-c s r ('skg-set-relRepo').
***** off a relationship
"Not on a headline"; "Not on an occurrence, an unknown viewnode or a
restricted viewnode" (on a folder, a ghost or a tombstone, say);
"Root headline: there is no relationship here to set"; "The parent
headline is neither a node nor a writable folder"; and, on an alias,
"Alias has no owning node headline", where the alias folder stands
under no headline.
***** an ID missing
"No id in this headline's metadata", "No id in the parent headline's
metadata", and, under a folder, "Could not find the folder's
viewparent".
***** a write-protected position
"Cannot set the relationship's repo from this write-protected FOLDER
position", on a member of a folder whose membership the save does
not read (the relationship belongs to the other end there); "The
parent is write-protected here, ...", under a write-protected
occurrence; "The folder's viewparent is write-protected here, ...",
under an editable folder of a write-protected occurrence.
***** a pending edit request
"Cannot request a relRepo where a delete, merge or flag request is
pending": the headline already holds one of those, which takes the
edit request's one slot.
*** <localleader>sR : :SkgSetRelRepoRecursive
Like 'SetRelRepo', but applied throughout the subtree at point (the
node at point's own relationship to its viewparent included).

It first asks, with Neovim's selection menu, which role the
view-children should play toward their viewparents: one entry per
role of the schema's four node-node relations. Only two roles are
settable from the child's position -- =content= (ordinary content)
and =forkee= (a claiming forksFolder member); choosing any other role
says why its relationship cannot be set from there.

It then prompts for a skgrepo over every skgrepo, plus the
no-override choice, which instead removes the pending requests
throughout the subtree. No per-relationship default is fetched, so
the save's floor check validates each relationship.

The walk recurses only on viewchildren that are members: member
occurrences, and the two editable folders. It sets an unknown
viewnode or a restricted viewnode too, where it stands as such a
member. It prunes below write-protected nodes and forkees as such, and prunes write-protected folders, ghosts and other
non-vognodes entirely. A pending delete, nodeMerge or flag request
anywhere in the walk refuses the whole gesture before any edit
("Cannot request a relRepo where a delete, merge or flag request is
pending"). Save the view afterward to apply the changes.
*** <localleader>sx : :SkgSetFlagSearchMatching
Prompts between =search matching= and =no search matching= and stages the
desired state without saving. Foreign/write-protected/unsaved roots and a
node that already holds an edit request (delete, a nodeMerge or a
flag) are refused. A processed request stays beside it. A pending
relRepo request gives way to it, and the message says so: "replaced a
pending relRepo request". ':SkgDelete' (<localleader>dd) and
':SkgSetMergeRequest' (<localleader>sm) replace a pending relRepo
request too, and a flag request, without saying so.
*** <localleader>sX : :SkgSetFlagSearchMatchingRecursive
Applies one selected state uniformly through the true-content
subtree ('docs/glossary.org', "true-content subtree"),
deduplicating PIDs and reporting ineligible descendants; the message
counts the pending relRepo requests it replaced. It prunes non-vognodes,
branches carrying =noClaim=, ghosts, unknown viewnodes and restricted
viewnodes. Save with
=:w= afterward.
*** <localleader>sm : :SkgSetMergeRequest
(See [[./merging.org][the docs on merging]] for why would you merge two nodes,
and what it means to do that.)

Run this from the acquirer node.
It prompts for the acquiree, accepting either a bare ID
or an org link like =[[id:ID][label]]=,
and edits the acquirer's metadata to request a nodeMerge.

The command only edits the node's metadata in the current buffer.
Save the view afterward to apply the nodeMerge.
Other edits in the same save, to either node or elsewhere, are kept,
but a save that also deletes the acquirer or the acquiree is refused.
*** <localleader>sn : :SkgRestoreDeletedNode
In a buffer of the diff view, on a ghost (a node deleted since HEAD,
shown =ᗣ☮ ∃-=), requests that the save write the node back
as HEAD had it: its file in its home skgrepo, its own relationships
included, and its place in each list that recorded it at HEAD (at its
index there, in the skgrepo that recorded it), unless that recorder is
itself deleted. The headline shows =restore node= until the save. On
any other headline it refuses at once, with "Only a node deleted
since HEAD can be restored; restoreNode belongs on a ghost
(:SkgRestoreDeletedNode)". It does not save. Save with =:w=
afterward to apply it. See "Restoring what a change removed" in
[[./diff-view.org][the diff view's docs]].
*** <localleader>sl : :SkgRestoreRemovedMembership
In a buffer of the diff view, on a removed member, or on a member of
a partner folder whose relationship to the folder's viewparent was removed
(=~-=), editable or write-protected, requests that the save re-add that
one relationship as HEAD recorded it. The headline shows =restore
membership= until the save. On a ghost it refuses with
"This node is deleted; restore it first (:SkgRestoreDeletedNode)",
and on any other headline that is not a removed membership with
"Only a removed membership can be restored", at once. It does not
save. Save with =:w= afterward to apply it. A relationship whose other end is still deleted
is not restored; the save says so.
** <localleader>r : the diff view: extending, committing, moving between changes
These act on the buffers of the diff view (<localleader>vd). Marking
its changes processed is <localleader>m ("<localleader>m : processed
marks, in the diff view").
*** <localleader>ru : :SkgDiffViewExtend
Extends the buffer of the diff view to every change not editable in it.
Each changed node with no editable occurrence becomes editable where
the buffer first shows it, in content or else in a partner folder,
with its change and its content shown under it; when a change is
under a root the buffer lacks, that root is appended at the end. A
notification then shows the processed summary, as after a save.
Refuses with "Save the buffer first." while the buffer has unsaved
changes. A clean buffer the server rerenders after reloading files
changed on disk is extended the same way, with no key pressed.
(Emacs: C-c r u.)
*** <localleader>rc : :SkgStageAndCommit
<localleader>rc commits every node whose changes are all processed,
except one that needs a node whose changes are not. A node's changes
are its own (its text, aliases, extra IDs, flags, home skgrepo, its
existence) and those of its lists, so a child's ~ is its container's
change. A node goes in whole, all its '.skg' files or none, in each
owned skgrepo (one git-commit per skgrepo); foreign skgrepos are never
committed. A processed node waits, uncommitted and still marked, while
it needs a node that does not go in: it names a new node that does
not, it is deleted and a node that does not go in still names it, or
it is part of a merge whose other parts do not all go in.

A node one of whose files, at HEAD or now, is not what skg writes for
it (another field order, say, which only a hand edit makes) is not
processed, so <localleader>rc leaves it out, however many of its
marks are set: its file may have changed in a way the diff view does
not show, and no mark covers. Such a node goes in only with
<localleader>rC, or with Git.

It opens the buffer 'skg://commit-message' in a split, in which you
write the commit message. There ':w' or '<localleader>cc' commits
with that message and closes the split; '<localleader>ck' cancels and
deletes the buffer. The buffer remembers whether <localleader>rc or
<localleader>rC opened it last, and the notification on opening says
which commit it makes. The message is sent as written, less its
trailing whitespace; a blank one is refused. Nothing is asked. The
notification afterward says what went in and what is left, and names
each processed node that waits and what it waits for: "Committed 2
nodes, in public (9c1e40d), private (41aa07f). 2 changed nodes are
left; 1 of them is processed but waits: 'Plans for spring' names 'Seed
order', which is new and does not go in." It names each node left
because it changed in a way no mark covers, and how: "...; 1 of them
changed in a way no mark covers, which <localleader>rC or Git can
commit: 'Spring' (its file changed in a way the diff view does not
show (formatting, say))." When nothing is processed it says "Nothing is processed,
so nothing was committed; <localleader>rC commits everything."

After sending, the buffer keeps the message until it is moot: once
something is committed, or nothing had changed and nothing failed,
the buffer is deleted. When nothing is committed otherwise (nothing
processed, everything processed waiting, a "yes" declined, a refusal,
an error), the message stays there, and <localleader>rc or
<localleader>rC reopens it. What was staged in git by hand never goes
in, and stays staged: a commit is HEAD's tree plus the committed
nodes' files. Every open view must be saved or reverted first.
Afterward the open buffers of the diff view are rerendered: each
keeps its roots, its folding and what it made editable, and what was
committed no longer shows as a change. The commit lapses the marks of
everything it committed; every other mark stays.
(Emacs: C-c r c.)
*** <localleader>rC : :SkgStageAndCommitEverything
Commits every changed node of the owned skgrepos, processed or not,
with a message written in the same buffer as <localleader>rc's, by
the same commit, so nothing waits. If some changed node is not
processed, it first shows the processed summary and proceeds only if
you type the word "yes"; any other answer, or an interrupt, leaves
everything as it was and says "Not committed; your message is kept in
skg://commit-message". (Emacs: C-c r C.)
*** <localleader>rnc : :SkgDiffViewGotoNextChange
Moves the cursor to the next headline with change facts after it: a headline
whose metadata carries a '(leaves ...)' change fact, the server's count of
the changes it names. It skips a ☮ occurrence (not a ghost) standing directly in a
folder labelled "... (other files)" (its other containers, mentioners
or hiders changed), and one standing in the forks folder born only of
forking the viewparent ('(birth (forks out 2))'): that member records
the relationship in its own file, and its change is drawn, and visited,
where its node stands editable. <localleader>rnC visits those too.
The cursor lands at the start of the headline's
line. It does not wrap: past the last one it says "No
further change" and leaves the cursor, or, when only skipped ones are
left, "No further change but ☮ ones in "(other files)" folders;
<localleader>rnC visits them". It works in any skg buffer;
outside the diff view no headline names a change, so it finds none.
In a diff view extended to every change (<localleader>ru), it reaches
every change. In one not extended, a node shown only as such a ☮
member has its change shown only there, and only <localleader>rnC
reaches it; the processed summary counts such changes as not editable
in this view.
*** <localleader>rnu : :SkgDiffViewGotoNextUnprocessedChange
The same, visiting only headlines with change facts that are not
processed: a headline counts as processed when every change it names
is marked. Past the last
one it says "No further unprocessed change".
*** <localleader>rnp : :SkgDiffViewGotoNextProcessedChange
The same, visiting only processed headlines with change facts. Past the last one it
says "No further processed change".
*** <localleader>rpc : :SkgDiffViewGotoPreviousChange
Like <localleader>rnc, backward: moves the cursor to the previous
headline with change facts before it. Before the first one it says "No earlier
change".
*** <localleader>rpu : :SkgDiffViewGotoPreviousUnprocessedChange
Like <localleader>rnu, backward. Before the first one it says "No
earlier unprocessed change".
*** <localleader>rpp : :SkgDiffViewGotoPreviousProcessedChange
Like <localleader>rnp, backward. Before the first one it says "No
earlier processed change".
*** <localleader>rnC : :SkgDiffViewGotoNextChangeAnywhere
Like <localleader>rnc, visiting the headlines it skips too: every
headline with change facts. Each of the six motions has such a twin,
its last letter capital, ending in 'Anywhere'; at the end each says
what its plain twin says, naming no other key.
*** <localleader>rnU : :SkgDiffViewGotoNextUnprocessedChangeAnywhere
Like <localleader>rnu, skipping nothing.
*** <localleader>rnP : :SkgDiffViewGotoNextProcessedChangeAnywhere
Like <localleader>rnp, skipping nothing.
*** <localleader>rpC : :SkgDiffViewGotoPreviousChangeAnywhere
Like <localleader>rpc, skipping nothing.
*** <localleader>rpU : :SkgDiffViewGotoPreviousUnprocessedChangeAnywhere
Like <localleader>rpu, skipping nothing.
*** <localleader>rpP : :SkgDiffViewGotoPreviousProcessedChangeAnywhere
Like <localleader>rpp, skipping nothing.
** <localleader>m : processed marks, in the diff view
In a buffer of the diff view (<localleader>vd), each change can
be marked processed. A mark approves the change as it is now:
editing the changed thing again makes the mark lapse. Marks live on
the server, in a file beside its config
('<data_root>/processed-marks-CONFIGSTEM.json', unless the config names
another). A headline whose
change is processed shows ✓ after it; a processed aggregate (a
folder of changes, a changeset marker) shows ✓ when all of its changes are. A node that
existed at HEAD and has changes of its own (its text, home skgrepo,
aliases, extra IDs, flags, other changes such as a reordered list)
shows M ("modified"), and M✓ once those are
marked (<localleader>mnp); a node whose only change is which children it contains
shows no M, its children's ~ showing those changes.

A node's other changes, the ways its files changed that no other
headline shows (its text moved between a private and a public
section, its attribution changed, an alias moved to another skgrepo,
one of its lists was reordered, or something else in its file
changed), are one headline under it, just above its content, which
says them in those words: "its content was reordered". For a
reordered list its body shows the old order against the new, a line
a member, '-' at HEAD and '+' now. n marks it. The mark covers the
order (or attribution, or section) it was made on: change it the same
way again and the mark lapses.

After every save of one of the diff view's buffers, a
notification shows the processed summary, in nodes, the unit
<localleader>rc commits: "12 of 14 changed nodes are processed (1 of
them waits)", or "Commit ready. All 14 of 14 changed nodes are
processed." "Commit ready" means <localleader>rc would commit every
changed node. A changed node counts as processed when every change it
records is marked, its other changes among them; a processed node waits when <localleader>rc
would hold it back (see <localleader>rc). The summary
adds how many changes are not editable in this view (<localleader>ru
extends the diff view to them) and how many nodes changed in foreign
skgrepos.

A gesture that would unmark more than one change (a recursive one, one
on a folder of changes, or one on a modified node, which unmarks every
change of the node itself) first asks "Unmarking this node processed
will unmark every contributing decision. You might discard a lot of
hard-won information. Continue (yes/no)?", and does nothing unless
you type "yes". Unmarking a single change asks nothing. The
server counts the changes: each headline that names changes says how
many, in its metadata's '(leaves N ...)'. Where the client cannot
count them (what the server walks to, the changes a changeset marker's
members make), unmarking always asks.

Each mark is said directly: <localleader>m, then what (n the node, r
its relationship to the headline above it, b both), then which way (p
processed, u unprocessed); the Emacs keys are C-c m and the same
letters. A headline shows two things that can change: its node (∃+
new, ∃- deleted, M modified) and its relationship to the headline above
it (~+, ~-). On a modified node, n marks the changes of the node
itself: its text, home skgrepo, aliases, extra IDs, flags and other changes, not the
containment of its children, which each child's own ~ shows and r
marks. A headline that is one change (an old text, an alias, an ID, a
flag, a home-skgrepo move, a node's other changes) is marked by n or b; an unknown node's membership, or a
relationship moved to another skgrepo, by r or b. On a changeset marker ("its content
changed"), r marks the changed memberships it stands for and n the
changes of those members themselves. On a folder of changes, the
letter acts on each member, one level down. When the letter names
nothing on the headline, it says so and does nothing.

Neovim has no prefix argument. A capital last letter ('mnP', 'mbU')
is Emacs's C-u: the mark acts on every headline in the subtree at
point the letter names something on, and at a new node (∃+) that is
not in a folder it leaves the rest of that subtree to the server,
which marks the new node and each new node the graph says it
contains, and each new node those contain, and so on, whether or not
the buffer shows them, write-protected or not: with n their
existence, with r their content relationships (and the new node's own
relationship to the headline above it), with b both. A capital 'M'
('Mnp', 'Mbu') is Emacs's C-u C-u: the server instead follows every
relationship each new node records (contains, forks, hides). Every mark works on write-protected headlines too.
*** <localleader>mnp : :SkgMarkNodeProcessed
Marks the node at point processed, then saves: the changes of the node
itself, not its relationship to the headline above it. (Emacs: C-c m n p.)
*** <localleader>mnu : :SkgMarkNodeUnprocessed
As <localleader>mnp, but unmarks. (Emacs: C-c m n u.)
*** <localleader>mnP : :SkgMarkNodeProcessedContentward
As <localleader>mnp, on the subtree, new nodes walked contentward
(see the preamble). (Emacs: C-u C-c m n p.)
*** <localleader>mnU : :SkgMarkNodeUnprocessedContentward
As <localleader>mnP, but unmarks. (Emacs: C-u C-c m n u.)
*** <localleader>Mnp : :SkgMarkNodeProcessedOutward
As <localleader>mnP, new nodes walked along every relationship
they record. (Emacs: C-u C-u C-c m n p.)
*** <localleader>Mnu : :SkgMarkNodeUnprocessedOutward
As <localleader>Mnp, but unmarks. (Emacs: C-u C-u C-c m n u.)
*** <localleader>mrp : :SkgMarkRelProcessed
Marks processed the relationship of the headline at point to the
headline above it (its ~), then saves. (Emacs: C-c m r p.)
*** <localleader>mru : :SkgMarkRelUnprocessed
As <localleader>mrp, but unmarks. (Emacs: C-c m r u.)
*** <localleader>mrP : :SkgMarkRelProcessedContentward
As <localleader>mrp, on the subtree, new nodes walked contentward
(see the preamble). (Emacs: C-u C-c m r p.)
*** <localleader>mrU : :SkgMarkRelUnprocessedContentward
As <localleader>mrP, but unmarks. (Emacs: C-u C-c m r u.)
*** <localleader>Mrp : :SkgMarkRelProcessedOutward
As <localleader>mrP, new nodes walked along every relationship
they record. (Emacs: C-u C-u C-c m r p.)
*** <localleader>Mru : :SkgMarkRelUnprocessedOutward
As <localleader>Mrp, but unmarks. (Emacs: C-u C-u C-c m r u.)
*** <localleader>mbp : :SkgMarkBothProcessed
Marks processed both the node at point and its relationship to the
headline above it, then saves: everything the headline shows. (Emacs: C-c m b p.)
*** <localleader>mbu : :SkgMarkBothUnprocessed
As <localleader>mbp, but unmarks. (Emacs: C-c m b u.)
*** <localleader>mbP : :SkgMarkBothProcessedContentward
As <localleader>mbp, on the subtree, new nodes walked contentward
(see the preamble). (Emacs: C-u C-c m b p.)
*** <localleader>mbU : :SkgMarkBothUnprocessedContentward
As <localleader>mbP, but unmarks. (Emacs: C-u C-c m b u.)
*** <localleader>Mbp : :SkgMarkBothProcessedOutward
As <localleader>mbP, new nodes walked along every relationship
they record. (Emacs: C-u C-u C-c m b p.)
*** <localleader>Mbu : :SkgMarkBothUnprocessedOutward
As <localleader>Mbp, but unmarks. (Emacs: C-u C-u C-c m b u.)
*** <localleader>mhp : :SkgMarkHomeSkgrepoMoveProcessed
Marks processed the home-skgrepo move of the node at point (or the
move at point), then saves. (Emacs: C-c m h p.)
*** <localleader>mhu : :SkgMarkHomeSkgrepoMoveUnprocessed
As <localleader>mhp, but unmarks. (Emacs: C-c m h u.)
*** <localleader>mhP : :SkgMarkHomeSkgrepoMoveProcessedRecursive
Also marks every descendant whose home skgrepo moved between the same
two skgrepos. (Emacs: C-u C-c m h p.)
*** <localleader>mhU : :SkgMarkHomeSkgrepoMoveUnprocessedRecursive
As <localleader>mhP, but unmarks. (Emacs: C-u C-c m h u.)
** <localleader>m : other graph modifications
*** <localleader>ma : :SkgReceipt
On the headline of an item in a view of someone's mailbox to you
(or anywhere in its body), write a read receipt: say how you handled
the item, and file it away. It asks for one line, "Read." by default
(an empty answer), and then the server, in one write, puts a new note titled
"Read.", that line its body, as the first child of your fork of the
item (forking it first if you hold no fork of it; no fork
confirmation is asked), and hides the item from your fork of the
mailbox, so that it leaves the unread items. A notification says what
it wrote and hid; the views that show them are redrawn.

Where the item is in several mailboxes you read, it asks which to
hide it from; where it is in none it hides nothing, and says so, as
where it is already hidden. A new fork goes where your fork of the
mailbox is, if the item is homed in the mailbox's skgrepo; otherwise
it asks for the skgrepo, so that an item from a more private skgrepo
of its owner is not forked into a public one by default.

Refuses while the buffer has unsaved edits, which the redraw would
replace; other buffers with unsaved edits are not redrawn. See
=docs/forks.org=, "Read receipts".
*** <localleader>mc : :SkgReplaceLinkWithContent
Replace the leaf at point with a content relationship to the
node it links to, then save the buffer.

Point can be on the headline or in the node body. The node at
point can be new or already in the graph. If it already has an
ID, the command warns that the old node might become an orphan graphnode.

The headline title plus body must contain exactly one org bracket
link, and that link must be an =id:= link. The node must have no
viewdescendants. Its viewparent must be an editable occurrence
whose skgrepo is owned in =skgconfig.toml=.

The command replaces the whole leaf with a same-level
write-protected occurrence for the link target. The parent is
editable, so saving records the dest as content of the
parent; the replacement child is write-protected, so its own text is
not rewritten from the link label.
*** <localleader>mf : :SkgFork
Fork the node at point that you already own: create a private
clone that forks it. This is the explicit counterpart to the
implicit fork (which is triggered by editing a /foreign/ node);
use it to deepen a fork chain, e.g. to layer a private =D=
over a public clone =C= that already forks a foreign =N=.

Refuses if the buffer has unsaved changes ("Save the buffer
before forking."), so the clone's saved state matches what you see.
Otherwise it stamps the node and auto-saves; the server returns
the usual fork-confirmation buffer (=skg://fork-confirmation=).
There you must set the clone's skgrepo with 'SetRepo'
(<localleader>ss) (it starts as the placeholder PICK-A-REPO,
with your first-declared owned skgrepo suggested above it), then
approve with <localleader>cc; or decline with <localleader>ck
(which also strips the fork request so the next save does not
re-fork). ':w' on the fork-confirmation buffer refuses and points
you back at these two keys.

The clone forks the node, and the original
keeps its own (owned) content. A node may have at most one clone
you own; forking an already-forked node is rejected, naming the
existing clone. See =docs/forks.org=.
*** <localleader>ml : :SkgReplaceContentWithLink
Replace the branch at point with a link to the node that used to
be there, then save the buffer.

Point can be on the headline or in the node body.
The command uses the headline either way.

The node being replaced must be an existing occurrence with an ID,
and a viewchild of an editable occurrence whose skgrepo is
owned in =skgconfig.toml=. The command acts locally,
replacing only this occurrence in the current buffer:
the headline at point and all of its viewdescendants,
including non-vognodes, ghosts, unknown viewnodes and restricted viewnodes,
are removed from the view and replaced by a same-level headline
whose title is an =[[id:...][...]]= link to the original node.

If the original headline title already contains a link, the
command asks before proceeding: "Are you sure you want to make that title, which contains a link, into a link? (There's nothing wrong with that, and sometimes it's appropriate, but it can be confusing.)"
** <localleader>v : view-level commands
*** <localleader>vb : :SkgOrgBodyToggle
Toggles the visibility of the body of the headline at point without
folding its children. If the whole headline is folded, the command
shows its body and immediate children, but leaves each child's
subtree folded. Works from the headline or from inside its body;
called from the body, the cursor moves to the start of the headline.
A bodyless headline is left alone unless its children need to be
revealed. A one-line body cannot be folded, since vim cannot close a
one-line fold; the command says so and leaves it shown.
*** <localleader>vd : :SkgDiffViewOpen
If you use git to manage your data,
this opens the diff view: every change in the owned skgrepos
since their last commits (how each worktree differs from HEAD), with
the context needed to understand it. It opens up to four buffers,
"skg://diff-view: all changes", "...: merges", "...: skgrepo changes"
and "...: order-only changes", skipping any that would be empty. It
refuses unless the connection is unrestricted, and when an owned
skgrepo is not in a git repository or has no HEAD commit (the refusal
names the skgrepo). As each buffer opens, a notification shows its
processed summary, as after a save (see <localleader>m).

Once the diff view's buffers are open, a switch of the
skgrepo restriction (':SkgRestrictRepoSet', <localleader>vl)
rerenders them under the new one: a buffer of the diff view then
draws no ghost of a graphnode the skgrepo restriction keeps out, and
draws such a graphnode, where a visible relationship names it, as a
restricted viewnode carrying only that relationship's change (=~+=
or =~-=), as <localleader>vl below says.

A buffer keeps its roots until you close it, but
for a ghost root whose deletion a commit records: it becomes a
tombstone, which keeps what stood under it and goes when it holds
nothing. Saving it (or committing) keeps what you folded. A save (of it or of
another view) decides what it adds anew by what changed: a new member
that changed, or leads to a change, is editable with its content, and
any other new member is a write-protected member shown without its
content. But a
save makes nothing editable that the buffer already shows, and
appends no root: the processed summary counts a change since the
buffer opened that it holds nowhere editable as not editable in this
view. <localleader>ru extends the buffer to such changes.
Nothing the buffer holds editable is write-protected again by the
server. An editable-view
request (<localleader>se) works as in any view, except that
'initial_node_limit' refuses only the extension of a node outside U
(the nodes the buffer extends anyway: those that changed and those
leading to them). Every node of U drawn editable counts toward it,
as does every other extension in the buffer, but no node of U is
ever refused, and nothing else in the buffer is bounded by that
limit.
Why a commit takes whole nodes, and never a set of files: the graph
is one structure spread over many files, so committing some changed
files and not others can leave HEAD inconsistent: it can name nodes
it does not contain, or hold a moved node in two skgrepos at once, or
in none. Such a HEAD cannot be reasoned about, and the next diff view
against it reports changes that are only its own inconsistency. So a
commit takes whole nodes, all their files in every owned skgrepo,
holds back a node that needs one that does not go in, and before
committing anything checks that the commit would read back as a
valid graph differing from the worktree by exactly the changes left
out; otherwise nothing is committed. Review with the processed marks
(<localleader>m), and commit what you have processed with
<localleader>rc.
The merges buffer shows each nodeMerge since HEAD: the acquiree and
its acquirer, in context. The acquiree's text preserver appears as a
new member of the acquirer's content. The skgrepo
changes buffer shows the nodes whose home skgrepo changed and the
nodes that record a relationship whose relRepo changed, each with all
of its changes; a moved node's
heralds read "-OLD +NEW", followed by "Δ⌂=a" when its nearest moved
ancestor (a, the viewparent; b, the grandparent; ...) moved the same
way. The order-only buffer lists the nodes whose only change is the
order of some list, each with its other changes, which show the old
order against the new and take the mark, then its content in the new
order. The all-changes buffer shows them too.
*** <localleader>ve : :SkgViewNewEmpty
Opens a blank Skg content view in which to create new nodes.
**** why
Every node needs a skgrepo.
A headline inherits one from the nearest occurrence above it,
passing through folders, ghosts, tombstones, unknown viewnodes and
restricted viewnodes; a root, or a headline whose walk up meets an alias, an
ID, a flag or a change viewnode first, or meets no occurrence,
needs its skgrepo chosen explicitly.
nvim-orgmode's insert-heading actions (org_meta_return and
org_insert_heading_respect_content) prompt for it when the new
headline cannot inherit one; '<localleader>ss' on a headline
typed by hand does the same.
Save validation catches a node whose skgrepo is missing.
*** <localleader>vh : :SkgHeraldsToggle
This command toggles it.
This toggles whether, at the start of every node,
metadata is shown in its full plain-text glory,
or is instead summarized via brief 'heralds'.
It is turned on at every view by default.
See [[./heralds.org][the herald legend]] for the tokens and styles.
*** <localleader>vL : :SkgToggleRepoOverlayOnLinks
Toggle display-only home skgrepo suffixes on Skg links in this buffer.
The suffixes start off. Links confirmed missing are ugly and underlined
even with suffixes off. See [[./heralds.org::*Link annotations][link annotations]].
*** <localleader>vl : :SkgRestrictRepoSet
Switches the skgrepo restriction of display and search for this
Neovim connection. The skgrepo restriction is two things: a
skgrepo-set, a prefix of the config's privacy ladder (the owned
skgrepos), and whether the foreign skgrepos are shown. Foreign
skgrepos have no place on the ladder; they are shown or hidden all at
once, apart from the rung, and are shown until you hide them.

The command asks for the most private owned skgrepo to show, which
activates it and every more public owned skgrepo, or for the foreign
skgrepos to be shown or hidden. The prompt, "Most private repo to
show, or foreign: shown/hidden (S-left/right cycle): ", lists the
owned skgrepos by name in privacy order, the most private as "NAME
(no restriction)", which is the default, then "foreign: shown" and
"foreign: hidden" (only when the config has a foreign skgrepo;
otherwise the prompt is "Most private repo to show (S-left/right
cycle): "); TAB completes and S-Left / S-Right cycles. Choosing a
skgrepo changes the rung and leaves the foreign skgrepos as they
were; choosing a foreign choice shows or hides them and leaves the
rung. It then asks "Switch the skgrepo restriction and re-render all
SKG buffers?", and on yes tells the server, and the server rerenders
every open Skg buffer in place. The confirmation reads "Skgrepo
restriction: NAME", with "; foreign repos hidden" while they are.
Choose the most private skgrepo, with foreign skgrepos shown, to
remove the skgrepo restriction.

Hidden, a foreign node is treated as any node outside the set, below:
an open view that showed it re-renders without it.

Under a skgrepo restriction, a node in a skgrepo outside the set
shows nothing of itself. Where a relationship recorded in a skgrepo
the set holds names such a node (say a public node contains a
private one), the view shows a headline with no title, heralded
=restricted=, standing for it: a restricted viewnode. It keeps the
relationship as it was when you save, and deleting its line removes
the relationship, as deleting an unknown viewnode does;
'<localleader>sr' sets its relRepo. A relationship recorded in a
skgrepo outside the set shows nothing at all, and a save keeps it. The
skgrepo restriction limits what you can edit as it limits what you can see:
a save never removes, moves or rewrites a relationship the set keeps
out, however the buffer looks, and never creates one silently. A save
that would record a relationship in a skgrepo the set keeps out (a
restricted viewnode pasted as content, a hide only a relationship
outside the set explains, '<localleader>sr' toward such a skgrepo) is refused, naming the
skgrepo. A fork copies into its clone only the relationships the set
shows; a node merge, like a delete, is refused when either node has a
section outside the set; a delete whose cleanup would strip
relationships outside the set asks first (see the delete). Restoring
from HEAD, processed requests and the cleanup of an absent ID's
references are refused unless the connection is unrestricted, and an
import into a skgrepo outside the set is refused. A
skgrepo narrowing (a switch to a smaller set) turns an open view's
headline of such a node into a restricted viewnode in place, its
children kept, and a skgrepo widening (a switch to a larger set)
turns the restricted viewnode back. Where nothing the set shows
names the node, its headline vanishes with what stood under it, and
so does a member whose record alone the set keeps out (a public node
that a private record says the headline's parent contains); a
skgrepo widening draws each again where the graph puts it. A view
root is the exception: a view rooted at such a node keeps its root,
as a restricted viewnode, whether or not anything the set shows
names it, since the view is your own request, and a
skgrepo widening makes it an occurrence again. The folders under a
headline that a skgrepo narrowing made a restricted viewnode (its
containers folder, say) describe a node it shows nothing of, so they
become tombstones, holding their members, and stay tombstones after
the skgrepo widening. A buffer of the diff view follows the same
rules (see <localleader>vd, ':SkgDiffViewOpen'). The switch reports none of this: it
says only "Skgrepo restriction: " and the name of the
skgrepo restriction.

The rerender redraws each open buffer from the view the server last
saved or rendered for it, which would lose an unsaved edit; so while
any view has unsaved edits the command refuses ("skg: save or revert
every skg view before switching the skgrepo restriction"), as stage-and-commit
does, and asks nothing.

If the proposed set would rerender overPrivateText telescope text, Skg asks before
changing the skgrepo restriction or any view. Declining leaves both unchanged and
an empty rerender stream releases the client's preemptive locks.

':SkgListRepoSets' shows the current skgrepo restriction and the
skgrepo-sets available, and ':SkgShowSkgrepoRestriction' shows the
skgrepo restriction alone, each marking the most private skgrepo
" (no restriction)": "Skgrepo restriction: public; available:
public, private (no restriction)".
*** <localleader>vm : :SkgViewMetadata
When called from a node in a view of the graph,
this switches to a view of the metadata of that node,
with one field per org branch. ':w' (or <localleader>cc) applies
the edited tree back into the source headline; ':bd!' cancels;
S-Left / S-Right cycle a field's value (writeProtected, noClaim,
editRequest, viewRequests, nodeRepo, ...).
Each field a user may set on the headline's kind is shown,
at its default when it is absent, and cycles through the values
that kind takes, as 'shared/metadata-fields.json' lists them:
a write-protected node is offered no delete, nodeMerge or flag request,
a removed member is also offered restoreRel,
a ghost restoreNode.
A value that needs more (a nodeMerge's target, relRepo's skgrepo,
a flag and its value, a folder's relation) prompts for it.
A field left at its default is dropped when the edit is applied.
A processed request the diff view's gestures wrote
(see <localleader>m) is shown in the edit request field, beside
the other request; deleting it there clears it.
After each headline, in parentheses, is the herald that field or
value gives a headline in a view, colored as there (once the server
has sent its herald rules); the hint is not text, and shows what
the editor opened with, not what cycling a value makes.
Metadata edited by hand, here or in the view itself, is checked
against the metadata grammar when you save: a headline whose metadata
breaks it refuses the save, and the refusal names the part that
breaks it.
It's easy to edit this way.
Note that some properties don't make sense to edit,
like the count of how many contents it has.
(If you want to change how much content a node has,
don't change the node's metadata; change its children in the view.)
*** <localleader>va : :SkgViewAncestry
If you're at a headline so deep in the tree
that you can't remember where it came from,
this brings you to a new view showing only that ancestry,
with heralds if the view you called it from shows them.
This actually works in org-mode outside of skg.
(skg uses org-mode, but org-mode can be used without skg.)
*** <localleader>vo : :SkgCyclePerspective
Show this view from the next perspective: the skgrepo whose list of
skgrepos ranks the mirrors it shows. Each switch names the
perspective it shows; it redraws the
buffer, and refuses while it has unsaved edits.

Where a node stands as another's content and it has mirrors (notes
